findings.title: Index creation will lock writes on the events table
findings.explanation: A plain CREATE INDEX takes a SHARE lock on the table, blocking all INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE for the duration of the build. Events is typically a large, write-heavy table, so this can cause an outage in production. Use CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY (Postgres) instead. Note that CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block, so make sure the migration tool is configured to run this migration without a wrapping transaction (e.g. a no-transaction directive or flag).

findings.title: Migration is not idempotent
findings.explanation: If a concurrent build fails, it leaves an INVALID index behind, and a rerun would then fail with 'relation already exists'. Use CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS, and document or script a DROP INDEX of any invalid index before retrying.

findings.title: No evidence the index matches the actual query or is used
findings.explanation: The PR does not show the query behind the endpoint or an EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) before and after. Please confirm the query filters on project_id and orders by id DESC (and any pagination uses id < cursor), so the planner can use this index without a sort. If the query also filters on other columns such as event type or a time range, a different or partial index may be better. Adding the EXPLAIN output to the PR description would help.

findings.title: Possible redundancy with existing indexes and write overhead
findings.explanation: Check whether an existing index on events(project_id) already exists. If so, the new composite index makes it redundant, and it should be dropped to save disk space and reduce write amplification on a high-insert table. Also consider the index size and the added insert cost.

findings.title: No rollback or down migration
findings.explanation: There is no corresponding DROP INDEX (down migration) in case the index causes regressions or the planner chooses it badly. If the project convention uses down migrations, add one, using DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS events_project_id_idx.

findings.title: Missing trailing newline / PR description wording
findings.explanation: Please verify the file ends with a newline. Also, the description says 'sequential scan per project', which is slightly imprecise; it is a sequential scan of the whole events table filtered by project. Clarifying this and including measured latency improvements would make the PR easier to evaluate.

## Speed up the project activity feed

The project events endpoint does a sequential scan per project. Adds an index on `events (project_id, id DESC)` to match the query.

## Diff

```diff
diff --git a/migrations/005_events_project_idx.sql b/migrations/005_events_project_idx.sql
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..0586576
--- /dev/null
+++ b/migrations/005_events_project_idx.sql
@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+CREATE INDEX events_project_id_idx ON events (project_id, id DESC);
```
